S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

patient_info.stressor: Tyler’s regional profile rose quickly after he won a competitive commission and was invited to conduct a premiere, an achievement that placed his scores, rehearsal decisions, and professional relationships under more public scrutiny than before. Across the following 1 year and 9 months, he developed increasingly fixed beliefs connected to the achievement and its aftermath, interpreting routine artistic feedback and scheduling decisions through a rigid personal explanation that colleagues could not disconfirm with emails, contracts, or rehearsal notes. Because his daily structure, marriage, running routine, and composing work remained largely intact, the issue was first treated as professional stubbornness rather than a psychiatric concern. He eventually sought care on his own after a musicians’ wellness seminar described how fixed, unshakeable beliefs can become clinically significant even when a person is otherwise functioning well.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m here because for almost two years I’ve been unable to shake the certainty that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work, even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Outside of this issue with the ensemble, I still meet deadlines, keep up with composing, run most mornings, and things at home with my wife are basically steady.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: The main consequence is that rehearsals and professional emails take more energy because I reread decisions and sometimes ask for extra clarification, but I haven’t lost work or stopped taking care of myself.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on since after I won the commission and was invited to conduct the premiere, about a year and nine months ago.
